title: Prosthetist and Orthotist Home Visit in Karachi
seoTitle: Prosthetist & Orthotist Home Visit in Karachi | Umeed Care Center
description: How home visits for artificial limbs, braces and insoles work in Karachi: who they suit, what happens at the visit, what to keep ready and how to book.
answer: Umeed Care Center has no walk-in outlet. A specialist comes to your home anywhere in Karachi to assess you, take measurements and fit your artificial limb, brace or insoles, and follows up at home after delivery. You book on WhatsApp at +92 313 6422564.

sections.heading: Who a home visit suits
paragraphs: A home visit is the easier option when travelling is hard. This includes people with a recent amputation, children who are anxious in hospitals, elderly patients, people using wheelchairs and families who cannot take a day off for several clinic trips.

sections.heading: What happens at the visit
paragraphs: The visit follows the same steps as any good fitting, only in your own space.
list: Assessment: we look at your condition, your reports and what you need to do each day.
Measurement: we measure or take a cast of the limb, foot or spine area.
Trial fitting: you try the device and we adjust it before it is finalised.
Delivery and follow-up: we hand over the finished device, teach you to use and care for it, and come back to adjust it if needed.

sections.heading: What to keep ready
paragraphs: Keep any earlier medical reports, X-rays or prescriptions, and the device you use now if you have one. If you have none of these, that is fine. We assess you in person.

sections.heading: Areas covered
paragraphs: We cover all of Karachi, including DHA, Clifton, Gulshan-e-Iqbal, North Nazimabad and Gulistan-e-Johar. If you live outside Karachi, message us your city and details and we will tell you what is possible.

sections.heading: How to book
paragraphs: Message us on WhatsApp at +92 313 6422564 with your area and a short description of the problem. The first consultation is free, and we confirm a time that suits you.

faqs.q: Do you have a clinic I can walk into?
faqs.a: No. Umeed Care Center is a home-visit service. Our team comes to you anywhere in Karachi.

faqs.q: Is the first consultation free?
faqs.a: Yes. The first consultation is free. The final price of a device is given after the assessment.

faqs.q: Can children be fitted at home?
faqs.a: Yes. Many children are calmer at home. Measurements, trial fitting and follow-ups for children are done the same way.

faqs.q: Do you only visit for a first fitting?
faqs.a: No. We also come back for adjustments, as a growing child or a changing limb often needs the fit checked.

title: KAFO Brace for Polio in Karachi: What It Is and Who Needs It
seoTitle: KAFO Brace for Polio in Karachi | Umeed Care Center
description: A plain guide to the KAFO (knee-ankle-foot orthosis) for polio and leg weakness: how it works, how it is made and what to expect when you get one in Karachi.
answer: A KAFO is a custom leg brace that supports the knee, ankle and foot together. It is used when muscle weakness, often after polio, makes the leg unable to hold the body safely. A specialist measures the leg, makes the brace to fit and checks the fit over follow-up visits.

sections.heading: What KAFO means
paragraphs: KAFO stands for knee-ankle-foot orthosis. It is a brace that runs from the thigh to the foot. Metal or plastic uprights and a shoe or foot section hold the leg in a stable position.

sections.heading: Why polio patients use it
paragraphs: Polio can leave a leg too weak to keep the knee straight under body weight. A KAFO with a knee joint that can lock gives the knee support when standing and walking, and can be unlocked to sit.

sections.heading: How a KAFO is made
list: Assessment of muscle strength, joint movement and walking.
Measurement or casting of the leg.
Fabrication to those measurements, with the knee joint and locking type chosen for your needs.
Trial fitting, then adjustments until the brace is comfortable and safe.
Gait practice and follow-up visits.

sections.heading: What to expect
paragraphs: A new KAFO feels heavy and unfamiliar for the first days. Skin redness that does not fade, pressure marks or pain mean the fit needs adjusting, so tell your specialist early instead of stopping use.

sections.heading: Children and growth
paragraphs: Growing children outgrow braces. Plan regular fit checks so the brace is adjusted or replaced as the child grows.

faqs.q: Can a KAFO help a polio patient walk without hand support?
faqs.a: Many people walk more steadily with a KAFO, but the result depends on strength in the hips and trunk and on the condition of the other leg. Some people still need a stick or crutches. Your specialist can tell you what is realistic after an assessment.

faqs.q: What is the difference between an AFO and a KAFO?
faqs.a: An AFO supports the ankle and foot. A KAFO also supports the knee. A KAFO is used when the knee itself is not stable enough.

faqs.q: Is a KAFO made to measure?
faqs.a: Yes. A KAFO is custom made from measurements or a cast of your leg.

faqs.q: Can a KAFO be fitted at home in Karachi?
faqs.a: Yes. Umeed Care Center does assessment, measurement, trial fitting and follow-up at your home anywhere in Karachi.

title: Clubfoot (CTEV) Braces and Denis Browne Shoes in Karachi
seoTitle: Clubfoot Braces & Denis Browne Shoes in Karachi | Umeed Care Center
description: What a clubfoot brace is, why it is worn after casting, how Denis Browne shoes work and what parents in Karachi should know about fit and follow-up.
answer: After clubfoot (CTEV) is corrected with casting, a foot abduction brace, often called Denis Browne shoes on a bar, keeps the feet in the corrected position so the deformity does not return. Your child's doctor sets how long and how many hours it is worn.

sections.heading: What clubfoot is
paragraphs: Clubfoot, or congenital talipes equinovarus (CTEV), is a condition present at birth in which one or both feet turn inwards and downwards. It is treated early, usually with gentle casting by a doctor.

sections.heading: Why a brace follows casting
paragraphs: Once the foot is corrected, it can slowly turn back. A brace holds the feet in the corrected position. Skipping the brace is a common reason the problem comes back, so families are usually asked to follow the schedule closely.

sections.heading: How the shoes and bar work
paragraphs: The child wears special shoes that attach to a bar. The bar keeps the feet turned outward at the angle the doctor sets. The bar length is matched to the width of the child's shoulders.

sections.heading: What parents should watch
list: Red marks or sores on the skin.
A shoe that is too tight or has become too small.
A child who cries or refuses the brace on most days.
Heels lifting out of the shoe.
paragraphs: Any of these means the fit should be checked. Children grow fast, so check the fit often.

sections.heading: Who decides the schedule
paragraphs: Your child's orthopedic doctor decides how long and how many hours the brace is worn. We make and adjust the brace to the prescription and check fit as your child grows.

faqs.q: What are Denis Browne shoes?
faqs.a: They are shoes attached to a bar that holds a child's feet at a set angle. They are used after clubfoot correction to keep the correction.

faqs.q: How long does a child wear the brace?
faqs.a: It depends on the child and the doctor's plan. The brace is often worn full time at first and then for part of the day or at night. Follow your doctor's schedule.

faqs.q: Can the brace be adjusted as my child grows?
faqs.a: Yes. Fit should be checked regularly, and the brace is adjusted or replaced as the foot grows.

faqs.q: Do you provide this at home in Karachi?
faqs.a: Yes. We do measurements, fitting and fit checks at your home anywhere in Karachi.

title: Artificial Leg Types in Karachi: Below-Knee, Above-Knee and Components
seoTitle: Artificial Leg Types & Components in Karachi | Umeed Care Center
description: Below-knee and above-knee artificial legs explained, with how sockets, knees and feet differ in cost and use, plus the typical price range in Karachi.
answer: A below-knee (transtibial) leg replaces the part under the knee. An above-knee (transfemoral) leg also replaces the knee joint, so it costs more and takes longer to learn. In Karachi, published ranges are about PKR 80,000 to 350,000 for below-knee and PKR 150,000 to 600,000 for above-knee, depending on components.

sections.heading: Below-knee leg
paragraphs: A below-knee leg keeps your own knee. It has a socket that fits the remaining limb, a pylon and a foot. Because the knee is yours, walking is usually easier to learn.

sections.heading: Above-knee leg
paragraphs: An above-knee leg adds a prosthetic knee. The knee type changes how stable and natural walking feels, from simple mechanical joints to more advanced ones. This is the main reason prices rise.

sections.heading: The three parts that decide cost and comfort
list: Socket: made to your limb. A good socket matters more than any other part, because a poor fit causes pain and sores.
Knee (above-knee only): affects stability and walking pattern.
Foot: ranges from a solid ankle foot to energy-return feet that suit more active use.

sections.heading: Typical price range in Karachi
paragraphs: Published ranges from Karachi providers are roughly PKR 80,000 to 350,000 for a below-knee leg and PKR 150,000 to 600,000 for an above-knee leg. Your exact figure depends on the socket, the knee and the foot, and is given after assessment. Our price guide explains what moves the price.

sections.heading: Matching the leg to your life
paragraphs: Tell your specialist how active you are, what surfaces you walk on and whether you work on your feet. A leg built for daily walking differs from one built for running or heavy work.

faqs.q: How much does an artificial leg cost in Karachi?
faqs.a: Published ranges are about PKR 80,000 to 350,000 for below-knee and PKR 150,000 to 600,000 for above-knee. The exact price depends on the components and is given after assessment.

faqs.q: Which is easier to learn, below-knee or above-knee?
faqs.a: Below-knee is usually easier, because you keep your own knee.

faqs.q: Why does the socket matter so much?
faqs.a: The socket is the link between you and the leg. If it fits badly, you get pain and skin problems whatever the other parts are.

faqs.q: Can I get a trial before the final socket?
faqs.a: Many fittings use a trial socket first so the fit can be corrected before the final one is made. Ask your specialist about this at the assessment.

title: How the Artificial Leg Process Works: Steps and Timeline
seoTitle: Artificial Leg Process & Timeline in Karachi | Umeed Care Center
description: The steps from first assessment to walking with an artificial leg, what affects how long it takes and why several adjustment visits are normal.
answer: Getting an artificial leg takes several steps: assessment, measurement or casting, a trial socket, the final leg, then adjustments and training. Time varies with the person and the limb, and several follow-up visits in the first months are normal because the limb changes shape.

sections.heading: The steps
list: Assessment: your health, the limb, and what you need to do each day.
Measurement or casting of the remaining limb.
Trial socket: a test socket so the fit can be checked and corrected.
Final leg: the socket, pylon and foot are assembled.
Training: learning to stand, balance and walk, and to care for the limb and the socket.
Follow-up: adjustments as the limb settles.

sections.heading: What affects the time
paragraphs: A recently healed limb changes volume for weeks or months, so the fit may need work more than once. Your general health, the level of amputation and how often you can attend sessions also change the pace.

sections.heading: Why adjustments are normal
paragraphs: Expect at least a few adjustment visits in the first months. This is normal and does not mean something went wrong. Pain, redness or skin breakdown should always be reported early.

sections.heading: Preparing before the first visit
paragraphs: Keep reports and prescriptions ready, look after the skin of the limb, and bring someone with you for the first fittings. Message us before the visit with your situation so the first meeting is spent on assessment.

faqs.q: How long does it take to get an artificial leg?
faqs.a: It depends on the person and the limb. The process has several steps, and a recently healed limb often needs more adjustments. Your specialist can give you a realistic plan after the assessment.

faqs.q: Why does my limb change after amputation?
faqs.a: Swelling goes down and the limb changes volume over weeks and months, so the socket may need refitting.

faqs.q: Do I need physiotherapy?
faqs.a: Gait training helps most people. It builds balance and confidence, and your specialist will guide you.

faqs.q: Can the whole process happen at home?
faqs.a: Yes. Assessment, measurement, trial fitting and follow-ups can be done at your home in Karachi.

title: Diabetic Foot Care: Therapeutic Shoes, Insoles and Offloading in Karachi
seoTitle: Diabetic Foot Shoes, Insoles & Offloading in Karachi | Umeed Care Center
description: How therapeutic footwear and custom insoles protect a diabetic foot, which warning signs need a doctor, and what offloading boots are for.
answer: In diabetes, nerve damage and poor circulation can stop you feeling pressure or injury, and a small sore can become an ulcer. Therapeutic shoes and custom insoles spread pressure away from risky spots. For an existing ulcer, a doctor may prescribe an offloading boot.

sections.heading: Why feet need extra protection
paragraphs: Reduced feeling means a blister or pressure spot may go unnoticed. Dry skin, calluses and foot deformity add to the risk. Footwear that fits badly is a common cause of sores.

sections.heading: What therapeutic footwear does
paragraphs: Therapeutic shoes and sandals have a deeper, wider toe area, soft inner surfaces and no hard seams. A custom insole is shaped to your foot to spread pressure and reduce load on sensitive areas.

sections.heading: Offloading boots
paragraphs: When an ulcer or a Charcot foot is present, a doctor may prescribe a boot that takes pressure off the injured area while it heals. This is medical treatment and should follow your doctor's advice.

sections.heading: See a doctor quickly if you notice
list: A sore, blister or cut that is slow to heal.
Redness, warmth or swelling in a foot.
Black or discoloured skin.
Fluid or a bad smell from a wound.

sections.heading: Daily habits
paragraphs: Check both feet every day, including between the toes. Never walk barefoot. Check inside shoes for stones or rough spots before putting them on.

faqs.q: Do all diabetic patients need special shoes?
faqs.a: Not all. People with reduced foot sensation, deformity, calluses, poor circulation or a past ulcer benefit most. A clinician can tell you whether you need them.

faqs.q: What is a custom insole?
faqs.a: It is an insole shaped to your foot from a scan or cast, to spread pressure away from sensitive spots.

faqs.q: Can therapeutic footwear heal an ulcer?
faqs.a: Footwear helps prevent ulcers. An existing ulcer needs medical treatment, and a doctor may add an offloading boot.

faqs.q: Is a home foot assessment available in Karachi?
faqs.a: Yes. We assess and fit footwear and insoles at your home anywhere in Karachi.

title: AFO vs KAFO vs Knee Brace: Which Leg Brace Do You Need?
seoTitle: AFO vs KAFO vs Knee Brace: Which Leg Brace? | Umeed Care Center
description: A side-by-side guide to AFO, KAFO and knee braces: what each supports, which conditions they suit and how to tell which one applies to you.
answer: An AFO supports the ankle and foot, for example in foot drop. A KAFO supports the knee, ankle and foot together, for example in polio or serious leg weakness. A knee brace supports only the knee, for example in ligament injury or arthritis. A specialist decides after an assessment.

sections.heading: AFO (ankle-foot orthosis)
paragraphs: An AFO sits inside a shoe and supports the ankle. It is commonly used for foot drop after stroke or nerve injury, and in cerebral palsy to improve how the foot lands when walking.

sections.heading: KAFO (knee-ankle-foot orthosis)
paragraphs: A KAFO adds support at the knee, with a joint that can lock. It is used when the knee cannot hold body weight safely, for example after polio.

sections.heading: Knee brace
paragraphs: A knee brace works on the knee alone. Types include hinged braces for ligament injury, and unloader braces that shift load away from a painful side in knee arthritis.

sections.heading: How to choose
list: Is the problem at the ankle or foot only? An AFO is often the answer.
Is the knee unstable as well? A KAFO may be needed.
Is it only knee pain or a knee injury? A knee brace may be enough.
paragraphs: This is a starting point, not a prescription. The right brace depends on strength, joint movement, weight and daily activity.

sections.heading: Ready-made or custom
paragraphs: Ready-made braces are cheaper and quicker and suit mild needs. Custom braces are made to your measurements and suit complex shapes, children and long-term use.

faqs.q: What is foot drop and which brace helps?
faqs.a: Foot drop is difficulty lifting the front of the foot when walking. An AFO is the usual brace for it.

faqs.q: Can I buy a brace without an assessment?
faqs.a: You can buy ready-made braces, but a wrong brace can cause discomfort or not help. An assessment avoids that.

faqs.q: How long do I wear a brace?
faqs.a: It depends on the condition. Some braces are worn during recovery, others long term. Your specialist explains the expected duration.

faqs.q: Do you make braces at home in Karachi?
faqs.a: Yes. We assess, measure and fit braces at your home anywhere in Karachi.

title: Scoliosis Brace for Children in Karachi: How Bracing Works
seoTitle: Scoliosis Brace for Children in Karachi | Umeed Care Center
description: How a scoliosis brace works, who needs one, how many hours it is worn and what to do if a child finds it hard to wear.
answer: A scoliosis brace is a custom spinal brace that is worn to stop a growing child's spinal curve from getting worse. It does not usually straighten the spine. The doctor decides if a brace is needed and for how many hours a day it should be worn.

sections.heading: What the brace is for
paragraphs: For a growing child with a moderate curve, a brace is used to hold the curve in place while the child grows, aiming to avoid surgery. It works only while it is worn.

sections.heading: Types
paragraphs: Many scoliosis braces are TLSO types, which wrap the trunk. Some are worn full time and some only at night. The doctor chooses the type based on the curve and the child's age and growth.

sections.heading: How it is made
list: The doctor's diagnosis and the X-ray are the starting point.
We measure or scan the trunk.
The brace is made to those measurements.
A trial fitting checks the fit and comfort.
An X-ray in the brace and regular reviews follow.

sections.heading: Helping a child wear it
paragraphs: Wearing the brace as prescribed is what makes it work. Loose clothing, a soft undershirt and a regular routine help. Talk to your specialist about skin marks, pain or any problem, since a good fit makes wearing easier.

sections.heading: Growth checks
paragraphs: As a child grows, a brace stops fitting. Regular checks make sure it still holds the curve.

faqs.q: Does a brace cure scoliosis?
faqs.a: A brace aims to stop the curve from getting worse during growth. It does not usually straighten an existing curve.

faqs.q: How many hours a day is a brace worn?
faqs.a: It depends on the brace type and the doctor's plan. Some are worn many hours a day and some only at night.

faqs.q: Can a child be fitted at home?
faqs.a: Yes. Measurements, trial fitting and fit checks are done at your home anywhere in Karachi.

faqs.q: Who decides if my child needs a brace?
faqs.a: The child's orthopedic doctor decides based on the X-ray and growth. We make the brace to that prescription.
